# Use case diagram syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-usecase/grammar/usecase.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Use case diagram syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `usecase-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 lexed and parsed use case diagrams with Chevrotain
(`usecase.tokens.ts`, `usecase.parser.ts`); the token rules below are its rules, in its order,
with its three modes.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive, except `include` and
`extend`.

The first rule that matches wins, except that a keyword gives way to a longer name (`actors`
is a name, `actor-x` is `actor`, `-` and `x`), and a name to a longer number (`1.5px`). An id
is ASCII letters, digits and `_` (`1`, `_x`, `TBD` and `endpoint` are ids; `my-node` and
`Användare` are not: put such text in a label, `A("Användare")`). Every statement ends its
line; `%%` comments are whole lines.

**Elements.** `actor User`, `actor A, B`, a use case `Login`, `Login(Sign in)` (an ellipse) or
`Login[Sign in]` (a rectangle), or a name in quotes, whose id is its text with each character
other than a letter, digit or `_` as `_` (`"Reset password"` is `Reset_password`). A name may be
followed by `@{ … }` metadata, a `<<stereotype>>` and `:::class` names, in that order. An end of
a relation that nothing declares is a use case. An item with `:::` names ends a list of actors:
a `,` after it adds a class name. A statement cannot start with the PlantUML words
`allowmixing`, `newpage`, `package`, `rectangle` or `skinparam` (any case), nor with a bare name
and `@{`, which is a metadata statement.

**Arrows.** `-->` (point), `<--` (point at the start), `--` (no marker), `--o`, `o--`, `--x`,
`x--`; more dashes make a point or plain arrow longer. `-- label -->` (or `-- label --`,
`--o`, `--x`), `<-- label --`, `o-- label --` and `x-- label --` carry a label; only exactly
`--` and `<--` take one. `..> : include`, `..> : extend` and `--|>` (generalization) relate
like ends. `A e1@--> B` names the relation `e1`.

**Metadata** `@{ key: value, … }`: the properties are separated by `,` or line breaks; after the
last one a `,`, a line break, `,` and a line break, or two line breaks may come before `}` (two
or more after a `,`, or three, start another property, as in mermaid@12).

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `usecase-beta` on its own line, then statements, each on a line of its own,
blank lines and whole-line `%%` comments.

```ebnf
usecase = Header NEWLINE { line } EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = USECASE ;
```

```ebnf
line = NEWLINE
     | COMMENT NEWLINE
     | statement NEWLINE ;
```

```ebnf
statement = AccTitle
          | AccDescr
          | Direction
          | actorStatement
          | Boundary
          | Note
          | Json
          | ClassDef
          | Class
          | Style
          | Metadata
          | entityStatement ;
```

`accTitle: …`, the accessible title (the last one wins).

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE_LINE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`, the accessible description (the last one wins).

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR_LINE
                   | ACC_DESCR_BLOCK ;
```

```ebnf
Direction @Direction = DIRECTION ( TD | TB | BT | LR | RL ) ;
```

```ebnf
id = IDENTIFIER
   | PLANTUML ;
```

```ebnf
keyword = USECASE
        | ACTOR
        | SYSTEM_BOUNDARY
        | END
        | DIRECTION
        | TD
        | TB
        | BT
        | LR
        | RL
        | NOTE
        | FOR
        | JSON
        | CLASS_DEF
        | CLASS
        | STYLE
        | INCLUDE
        | EXTEND
        | TRUE
        | FALSE ;
```

```ebnf
word = keyword
     | id ;
```

```ebnf
plain = LABEL_SOLID
      | MARKERLESS_SOLID ;
```

```ebnf
labelPart = word
          | NUMBER
          | AT
          | COMMA
          | COLON
          | HASH_COLOR
          | CSS_IDENTIFIER
          | CSS_ESCAPED_COMMA
          | DASH
          | DOT
          | PERCENT
          | CSS_PUNCTUATION
          | LABEL_PUNCTUATION
          | LABEL_SYMBOL ;
```

A label: a text in quotes, a Markdown text, or words and punctuation up to the `)`, `]`,
arrow or line end after it.

```ebnf
label = PLAIN_STRING
      | MARKDOWN_STRING
      | labelPart { labelPart } ;
```

`actor A`, `actor A, B`, `actor A --> B`.

```ebnf
actorStatement = ACTOR actorItems
               | ActorRelation ;
```

```ebnf
actorItems = { BareActor COMMA } Actor ;
```

```ebnf
ActorRelation @Relation = ACTOR Actor relationTail ;
```

```ebnf
Actor @Element = actorName [ metadata ] [ stereotype ] [ classSuffix ] ;
```

```ebnf
BareActor @Element = actorName [ metadata ] [ stereotype ] ;
```

```ebnf
actorName = id [ LPAREN label RPAREN ]
          | PLAIN_STRING
          | MARKDOWN_STRING ;
```

A use case, or a relation from an element. At a statement's start a bare name takes no
`@{ … }` (that is a metadata statement) and is not a PlantUML word.

```ebnf
entityStatement = Declaration
                | Relation ;
```

```ebnf
Declaration @Element = entityHead ;
```

```ebnf
Relation @Relation = Source relationTail ;
```

```ebnf
Source @Element = entityHead ;
```

```ebnf
entityHead = IDENTIFIER ( LPAREN label RPAREN | LBRACKET label RBRACKET ) [ metadata ] [ stereotype ] [ classSuffix ]
           | ( IDENTIFIER | PLAIN_STRING | MARKDOWN_STRING ) [ stereotype ] [ classSuffix ] ;
```

```ebnf
Target @Element = entityName ;
```

```ebnf
entityName = ( id [ LPAREN label RPAREN | LBRACKET label RBRACKET ] | PLAIN_STRING | MARKDOWN_STRING ) [ metadata ] [ stereotype ] [ classSuffix ] ;
```

```ebnf
relationTail = [ id AT ] arrow Target ;
```

```ebnf
arrow = DEPENDENCY_ARROW COLON ( INCLUDE | EXTEND )
      | GENERALIZATION
      | FORWARD_SOLID
      | BACKWARD_LABEL_SOLID
      | BACKWARD_SOLID
      | plain
      | FORWARD_CIRCLE
      | BACKWARD_CIRCLE
      | FORWARD_CROSS
      | BACKWARD_CROSS
      | LABEL_SOLID label ( FORWARD_SOLID | plain | FORWARD_CIRCLE | FORWARD_CROSS )
      | ( BACKWARD_LABEL_SOLID | BACKWARD_CIRCLE | BACKWARD_CROSS ) label plain ;
```

`@{ key: value, … }`: properties separated by `,` or line breaks.

```ebnf
metadata = METADATA_START { NEWLINE } [ property { separator property } [ COMMA [ NEWLINE ] | NEWLINE [ NEWLINE ] ] ] RBRACE ;
```

```ebnf
separator = COMMA { NEWLINE }
          | NEWLINE { NEWLINE } [ COMMA ] { NEWLINE } ;
```

```ebnf
property = ( id | PLAIN_STRING ) COLON ( id | PLAIN_STRING | TRUE | FALSE ) ;
```

```ebnf
stereotype = STEREOTYPE_START STEREOTYPE_TEXT STEREOTYPE_END ;
```

```ebnf
classSuffix = CLASS_SEPARATOR id { COMMA id } ;
```

`systemBoundary Id(title)` or `systemBoundary "title"`, then `@{ … }` and `:::` classes,
then one actor list or use case per line, and `end`.

```ebnf
Boundary @Boundary = SYSTEM_BOUNDARY boundaryName [ metadata ] [ classSuffix ] NEWLINE { boundaryLine } END ;
```

```ebnf
boundaryName = id [ LPAREN label RPAREN | LBRACKET label RBRACKET ]
             | PLAIN_STRING
             | MARKDOWN_STRING ;
```

```ebnf
boundaryLine = NEWLINE
             | COMMENT NEWLINE
             | ACTOR actorItems NEWLINE
             | Member NEWLINE ;
```

```ebnf
Member @Element = entityName ;
```

`Id@{ … }` (or a quoted name): metadata for an element or relation declared anywhere.

```ebnf
Metadata @Metadata = ( id | PLAIN_STRING | MARKDOWN_STRING ) metadata ;
```

```ebnf
Note @Note = NOTE FOR id label ;
```

```ebnf
Json @Json = JSON_DECLARATION_START JSON_OBJECT_LITERAL [ classSuffix ] ;
```

```ebnf
ClassDef @ClassDef = CLASS_DEF id { COMMA id } styles ;
```

```ebnf
Class @Class = CLASS id { COMMA id } id { COMMA id } ;
```

```ebnf
Style @Style = STYLE id styles ;
```

`fill:#f96, stroke-width:2px`: CSS declarations separated by `,` (`\,` inside a value).

```ebnf
styles = styleValue { COMMA styleValue } ;
```

```ebnf
styleValue = ( word | CSS_IDENTIFIER | plain word ) COLON styleComponent { styleComponent } ;
```

```ebnf
styleComponent = word
               | PLAIN_STRING
               | NUMBER
               | HASH_COLOR
               | CSS_IDENTIFIER
               | CSS_ESCAPED_COMMA
               | DASH
               | DOT
               | PERCENT
               | CSS_PUNCTUATION
               | COLON
               | LPAREN
               | RPAREN
               | LBRACKET
               | RBRACKET
               | LBRACE
               | RBRACE
               | AT
               | plain ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `comment`, `acc`, `jsonBody`, `stereotype`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | — | `(?<=^\|\n)[\t ]*(?=%%)` | push(comment) | At a line start, a `%%` line that comment removal left (`%%` alone): its blanks are skipped and the comment read in its own mode, so only a whole-line `%%` is a comment. |
| INITIAL | — | `(?<=^\|\n)[\t ]*(?=accTitle[\t ]*:\|accDescr[\t ]*(?::\|\{[^}]*\}))` | push(acc) | At a line start, `accTitle:`, `accDescr:` or `accDescr { … }`: read in their own mode. |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | MARKDOWN_STRING | `"`[\s\S]*?`"` |  | A Markdown text: a quote and a backtick, to a backtick and a quote; it may span lines. |
| INITIAL | UNCLOSED_MARKDOWN_STRING | `"`[\s\S]*` |  | A Markdown text never closed: the rest of the text. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\n` |  | A line break. |
| INITIAL | JSON_DECLARATION_START | `json[\t ]+\w+[\t ]*@[\t ]*(?=\{)` | push(jsonBody) | `json Id@{ … }`: a JSON object drawn as a table of its keys and values, read with `JSON.parse` (a repeated key keeps its last value and its first place). |
| INITIAL | USECASE | `usecase-beta(?!\w)` |  | `usecase-beta`: starts a use case diagram. |
| INITIAL | ACTOR | `actor(?!\w)` |  | `actor User`, `actor A, B`, `actor User --> Login`: actors, or one actor and a relation. |
| INITIAL | SYSTEM_BOUNDARY | `systemBoundary(?!\w)` |  | `systemBoundary Shop … end`: a frame around the actors and use cases declared in it, one per line; `@{ type: package }` draws it as a package. Boundaries do not nest and hold no relations. |
| INITIAL | END | `end(?!\w)` |  | `end`: closes a `systemBoundary`. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTION | `direction(?!\w)` |  | `direction LR`: the direction of the layout (the last one wins; `LR` by default). |
| INITIAL | TD | `TD(?!\w)` |  | `TD`: top to bottom (the same as `TB`). |
| INITIAL | TB | `TB(?!\w)` |  | `TB`: top to bottom. |
| INITIAL | BT | `BT(?!\w)` |  | `BT`: bottom to top. |
| INITIAL | LR | `LR(?!\w)` |  | `LR`: left to right. |
| INITIAL | RL | `RL(?!\w)` |  | `RL`: right to left. |
| INITIAL | NOTE | `note(?!\w)` |  | `note for Login "text"`: a note attached to an actor or use case. |
| INITIAL | FOR | `for(?!\w)` |  | `for`: in `note for`. |
| INITIAL | JSON | `json(?!\w)` |  | `json`: a JSON table, `json Id@{ … }`. |
| INITIAL | CLASS_DEF | `classDef(?!\w)` |  | `classDef hot fill:#f96`: a class of styles (`default` applies to every element). |
| INITIAL | CLASS | `class(?!\w)` |  | `class A, B hot`: adds class names to elements or relations with ids. |
| INITIAL | STYLE | `style(?!\w)` |  | `style A fill:#f96`: styles one element or relation with an id. |
| INITIAL | INCLUDE | `[Ii][Nn][Cc][Ll][Uu][Dd][Ee](?!\w)` |  | `include` (any case): in `A ..> : include B`, a use case includes another. |
| INITIAL | EXTEND | `[Ee][Xx][Tt][Ee][Nn][Dd](?!\w)` |  | `extend` (any case): in `A ..> : extend B`, a use case extends another. |
| INITIAL | TRUE | `true(?!\w)` |  | `true`: a metadata value. |
| INITIAL | FALSE | `false(?!\w)` |  | `false`: a metadata value. |
| INITIAL | IDENTIFIER | `(?:actor\|systemBoundary\|end\|direction\|TD\|TB\|BT\|LR\|RL\|note\|for\|json\|classDef\|c…` |  | A word that starts with a keyword and goes on (`actors`, `notes-x` is `notes`, `-`, `x`): an id. |
| INITIAL | GENERALIZATION | `--\\|>` |  | `--\|>`: generalization, between two actors or two use cases. |
| INITIAL | DEPENDENCY_ARROW | `\.\.>` |  | `..>`: include or extend, `..> : include`. |
| INITIAL | STEREOTYPE_START | `<<` | push(stereotype) | `<<`: a stereotype, `<<Human>>`, on its line. |
| INITIAL | CLASS_SEPARATOR | `:::` |  | `:::`: class names after an element, `A:::hot,big`. |
| INITIAL | FORWARD_SOLID | `--+>` |  | `-->` (and more dashes): an association with a point at the end. |
| INITIAL | BACKWARD_LABEL_SOLID | `<--(?!-)` |  | `<--`: an association with a point at the start; exactly `<--` may take a label. |
| INITIAL | BACKWARD_SOLID | `<--+` |  | `<---` and more dashes: a longer association with a point at the start. |
| INITIAL | FORWARD_CIRCLE | `--o` |  | `--o`: an association with a circle at the end. |
| INITIAL | BACKWARD_CIRCLE | `o--` |  | `o--`: an association with a circle at the start; it may take a label. |
| INITIAL | FORWARD_CROSS | `--x` |  | `--x`: an association with a cross at the end. |
| INITIAL | BACKWARD_CROSS | `x--` |  | `x--`: an association with a cross at the start; it may take a label. |
| INITIAL | LABEL_SOLID | `--(?!-)` |  | `--`: an association without markers; exactly `--` may start a label. |
| INITIAL | MARKERLESS_SOLID | `--+` |  | `---` and more dashes: a longer association without markers. |
| INITIAL | METADATA_START | `@\{` |  | `@{`: metadata, `A@{ type: hollow }`. |
| INITIAL | AT | `@` |  | `@`: after a relation's id, `A e1@--> B`. |
| INITIAL | LBRACE | `\{` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RBRACE | `\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LBRACKET | `\[` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RBRACKET | `\]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LPAREN | `\(` |  |  |
| INITIAL | RPAREN | `\)` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COMMA | `,` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | HASH_COLOR | `#[0-9A-Fa-f]+` |  | A colour such as `#f96`. |
| INITIAL | PLAIN_STRING | `"[^\n"]*"\|'[^\n']*'` |  | A text in quotes, `"…"` or `'…'`, on one line, without escapes. |
| INITIAL | CSS_IDENTIFIER | `[A-Z_a-z]\w*(?:-\w+)+` |  | A word and one or more `-` words, such as `stroke-width`: a CSS name, not an id. |
| INITIAL | NUMBER | `\d+\.\d+[A-Za-z]*` |  | A decimal before a name could take its digits: `1.5px`. |
| INITIAL | PLANTUML | `(?:[Aa][Ll][Ll][Oo][Ww][Mm][Ii][Xx][Ii][Nn][Gg]\|[Nn][Ee][Ww][Pp][Aa][Gg][Ee]\|…` |  | A PlantUML word, which no statement starts with: an id elsewhere. |
| INITIAL | IDENTIFIER | `\w+` |  | An id: ASCII letters, digits and `_`. |
| INITIAL | NUMBER | `\.\d+[A-Za-z]*` |  | A number such as `.5` or `.5em`. |
| INITIAL | CSS_ESCAPED_COMMA | `\\,` |  | `\,`: a comma inside a style value. |
| INITIAL | DASH | `-` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DOT | `\.` |  |  |
| INITIAL | PERCENT | `%` |  |  |
| INITIAL | CSS_PUNCTUATION | `[!#$&*+\/=?^_\|~]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LABEL_PUNCTUATION | `[;<>\\`]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LABEL_SYMBOL | `[^\t\n\r -~]+` |  | Text outside printable ASCII, such as `日本語`: only in labels. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |
| comment | COMMENT | `%%[^\n]*` | pop | A whole-line `%%` comment. |
| acc | ACC_DESCR_BLOCK | `accDescr[\t ]*\{[^}]*\}` | pop | `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description over lines, to the first `}`. |
| acc | ACC_TITLE_LINE | `accTitle[\t ]*:[^\n]*` | pop | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title, the rest of the line. |
| acc | ACC_DESCR_LINE | `accDescr[\t ]*:[^\n]*` | pop | `accDescr: …`: the accessible description, the rest of the line. |
| jsonBody | JSON_OBJECT_LITERAL | `\{(?:[^{}"]\|"(?:[^"\\]\|\\[\s\S])*"\|\{(?:[^{}"]\|"(?:[^"\\]\|\\[\s\S])*"\|\{(?:[^…` | pop | The object: braces and strings balanced (five levels deep here; the parser has no limit). |
| jsonBody | UNCLOSED_JSON_OBJECT_LITERAL | `\{[\s\S]*` | pop | An object never closed: the rest of the text. |
| stereotype | STEREOTYPE_END | `>>` | pop | `>>`: closes a stereotype. |
| stereotype | STEREOTYPE_TEXT | `(?=(?:(?!>>)[^\n])*?(?!>>)\S)(?:(?!>>)[^\n])+(?=>>)` |  | The stereotype's text, up to the first `>>` on its line; not blank. |
| stereotype | UNCLOSED_STEREOTYPE_TEXT | `(?!(?=(?:(?!>>)[^\n])*?(?!>>)\S)(?:(?!>>)[^\n])+>>)[^\n]+` | pop | The rest of the line, when no `>>` closes the stereotype on it (or its text is blank). The lookahead repeats `STEREOTYPE_TEXT` (which is tried first, so the lexer reads the same): a highlighter that tries a mode's ends before its other rules then still finds the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
